subject: Post-call: model selection + Redwood verified performance links
messages:
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Erin Baxter <erin@novanet.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 15:06:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call: model selection + Redwood verified performance links

Thanks again for the time earlier, Erin — good conversation. Quick recap and a concrete next step so we can get you a meaningful eval run: 

Recap of needs you shared:
- Primary use: contextual customer support assistant (long context, mixed structured data)
- Target p50 latency goal: <= 120ms at interactive load for 1–3 token/window responses; batch tps target during nightly re-runs ~800 TPS
- Quality priorities: factuality and instruction-following for mixed prompts; hallucination tolerance is low
- Constraint: must pass SOC2 + data residency in us-east region

Initial model fit recommendations (based on call + preliminary data shapes):
1) Redwood-Compact-8 (quantized int8) — suggested for low-latency interactive routes
   - Verified profile (live): TPS baseline: 950 TPS (seq=128), p50=42ms, p95=118ms on g4dn-type infra with continuous batching
   - Good tradeoff for cost-sensitive routes and high concurrency
2) Redwood-Instruction-XL (fp16) — suggested for high-quality, longer-context scorers / fallback
   - Verified profile: TPS baseline: 120 TPS (seq=512), p50=210ms, p95=460ms
   - Higher quality on instruction-following / long completion cases

What I’m proposing: run two short evals on your prompt set (attached) — one focused on interactive surface (Compact-8) and one on fallback scorer (Instruction-XL). I’ve attached a 120-prompt seed set that reflects the scenarios you described. Results will include Redwood-verified perf profiles (latency percentiles, token throughput), plus quality metrics (BLEU/ROUGE-type proxies we use, hallucination flags).

Files / links I’ve added for the run:
- Attached: novanet-prompt-set-v1.csv (seed prompts + labels)
- Public perf profile: https://redwood.ai/perf-profiles/rvp-2026-03-novanet (read-only)
- Eval workspace (internal drive): https://drive.redwood.ai/teams/sales/novanet/evals/2026-02-run-1

Next steps (suggested timeline):
- You: confirm the attached prompt set + any other high-priority prompts by EOD Mon (2/23)
- We: spin up two short runs (48 hours) and share perf + quality report by Wed (2/25)
- Optional: a quick canary plan to route 5% of traffic to Compact-8 for a week once you sign off

If this plan looks good I’ll also loop in our solutions engineer for a short test-run setup call (15–30m).

Best,
Dev

--
Dev Patel
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
dev_patel@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

From: Erin Baxter <erin@novanet.ai>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 21 Feb 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: model selection + Redwood verified performance links

Thanks, Dev — this is helpful. A few clarifying Qs before we confirm prompts: 

1) For the Compact-8 numbers you shared, are the p95 figures measured at sequence length 128 or 256? Our typical customer message + metadata ends up ~200–350 tokens after enrichment.
2) For the Instruction-XL fallback, can you include memory/KV cache sizing guidance for seq=512? We’re concerned about GPU memory overhead for the nightly scorer runs.

Also — we’ll want the prompts redacted for PII before they leave our systems. Can you confirm if Redwood can run the eval inside our VPC (private deployment) or will it be hosted? If hosted, we’ll need to route the prompt set to your intake process and have an NDA addendum in place. 

Will review the attached seed and get back with any edits by Mon.

—Erin
Erin Baxter
Director, Product — NovaNet AI
erin@novanet.ai

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Erin Baxter <erin@novanet.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 22 Feb 2026 11:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: model selection + Redwood verified performance links

Erin — great questions, answered inline below. Thanks for flagging PII.

1) Compact-8 p95 context: the p95=118ms number I quoted was measured at seq=128 under continuous batching; at seq=256 we see p95 climb to ~190ms on the same instance class. For your 200–350 token envelope, expect p95 in the 170–260ms range depending on concurrency. I’ll include a small table in the perf summary.

2) Instruction-XL KV/cache guidance: for seq=512 you should budget ~20–24GB GPU memory for the model instance (fp16) including KV cache headroom per concurrent session. If you run nightly batched scoring at 800 TPS, we recommend sharded scoring with 4 workers and batching windows to stay within memory limits.

PII / deployment: we can run the eval inside your VPC (Redwood Private) — that’s what most enterprise customers do for seed prompt runs where PII is present. Alternatively, we can accept a redacted prompt set to our hosted eval environment; in that case we'll need the NDA addendum signed. I’m attaching the perf summary PDF and the prompt CSV with a suggested redaction column.

Action items I’ve taken: 
- Attached: redwood-verified-perf-summary.pdf (includes seq-dependent p50/p95/p99 numbers and TPS baselines across common instance classes)
- Marked novanet-prompt-set-v1.csv with a REDACT? column for your team to approve
- Added an internal eval ticket and drive folder (link below)

If you confirm VPC eval, I’ll have our solutions engineer (Jonas) reach out for required IAM/network details and we’ll carve out a dedicated eval window. Proposed asap: start the VPC eval on Tue 2/24 to return results by Thu 2/26.

Regards,
Dev

- Estimated cost for the two-run eval (Compact-8 interactive + Instruction-XL scorer) ~ $3,200 (infra + engineering support). We can eat the solutions-engineer coordination hours if you prefer and apply as credit against a Dedicated commit.
